name: superio_enter
prose: Precondition: base is the I/O port address of the Super-I/O index/data pair. Postcondition: if request_muxed_region(base, 2, DRVNAME) fails, it prints an error with pr_err and returns -EBUSY without writing to any port; otherwise it writes SIO_UNLOCK_KEY (0x87) twice to port base with outb and returns 0, leaving the 2-port region reserved; the caller is expected to release it later (superio_exit writes SIO_LOCK_KEY and calls release_region).
note: reviewer reasons were only mechanical contract complaints (contract names/omits EBUSY); contract dropped because the function touches I/O ports. f71882fg.c:2080-2093, superio_exit at 2101-2105.

name: rpm_from_cnt
prose: Precondition: when cnt is not 0xff, p and clk_div are nonzero (otherwise the integer division is by zero) and (cnt ? cnt : 1) * p * clk_div, computed in signed int, does not overflow. Postcondition: it returns 0 when cnt == 0xff; otherwise it returns (clk_freq * 30 * gear_mult) / ((cnt ? cnt : 1) * p * clk_div) as an unsigned int, where the numerator is computed in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic (modulo 2^32 if it exceeds 4294967295). It reads no global state, takes no lock and allocates nothing.
contract: /*@ requires cnt == 255 || (p != 0 && clk_div != 0 && (cnt == 0 ? 1 : cnt) * p * clk_div <= 2147483647 && clk_freq * 30 * gear_mult <= 4294967295); ensures (cnt == 255 ==> result == 0) && (cnt != 255 ==> result == (clk_freq * 30 * gear_mult) / ((cnt == 0 ? 1 : cnt) * p * clk_div)); */
note: reviewer claim (gear_mult != 0 needed to avoid overflow of clk_freq*30) is wrong: g762.c:171-173 the numerator is u32 unsigned arithmetic, which wraps by definition, and with gear_mult == 0 the product is 0 either way; the real hazards are the signed denominator product and a zero denominator, now stated.

name: cnt_from_rpm
prose: Precondition: when rpm is nonzero, p and clk_div are both nonzero, so f2 = p * clk_div is nonzero (otherwise 255 * f2 or ULONG_MAX / f2 divides by zero). Postcondition: it returns 0xff when rpm is 0. Otherwise it computes f1 = clk_freq * 30 * gear_mult in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic (wrapping modulo 2^32), f2 = p * clk_div, replaces rpm by clamp_val(rpm, f1 / (255 * f2), ULONG_MAX / f2), and returns DIV_ROUND_CLOSEST(f1, rpm * f2) converted to unsigned char, i.e. reduced modulo 256 if the quotient exceeds 255. It takes no lock and allocates nothing.
note: g762.c:180-193. Old prose had the clamp and round-half-up right; contract dropped (clamp_val unbound in ACSL, rejected in every round). Width of unsigned long is architecture dependent.

name: ina209_to_reg
prose: Precondition: val is not LONG_MIN (it is negated for the INA209_CRITICAL_DAC_NEG case) and, for the power registers, DIV_ROUND_CLOSEST(val, 20000) fits in int, since the result is returned as int. Postcondition: depending on reg it returns: for INA209_SHUNT_VOLTAGE_POS_WARN and _NEG_WARN (0x0c, 0x0d) clamp(val, -320, 320) * 100; for INA209_BUS_VOLTAGE_OVER_WARN, _UNDER_WARN, _OVER_LIMIT and _UNDER_LIMIT (0x0f, 0x10, 0x12, 0x13) (DIV_ROUND_CLOSEST(clamp(val, 0, 32000), 4) << 3) | (old & 0x7); for INA209_CRITICAL_DAC_NEG (0x15) (clamp(-val, 0, 255) << 8) | (old & 0xff); for INA209_CRITICAL_DAC_POS (0x14) (clamp(val, 0, 255) << 8) | (old & 0xff); for INA209_POWER_WARN and INA209_POWER_OVER_LIMIT (0x0e, 0x11) DIV_ROUND_CLOSEST(val, 20000); for any other reg value -EACCES. It has no side effects.
note: ina209.c:154-195. Prose was already right; register numbers checked against the #defines at ina209.c:45-54. Contract dropped: long ternary form was rejected (unbalanced brackets, unbound DIV_ROUND_CLOSEST) and the -EACCES clause cannot be stated simply.

name: it87_find
prose: Precondition: sioaddr is the Super-I/O index port, address and sio_data point to writable storage, and chip_cnt indexes force_id when force_id_cnt != 1. Postcondition: it first calls superio_enter(sioaddr, true) (reserving the region without entering configuration mode) and returns that call's nonzero error immediately if it fails. After that it returns -ENODEV, with the chip left unrecognized or skipped, when DEVID reads 0xffff both before and after entering configuration mode, when the (possibly forced) chip id is 0xffff or not in the supported list, when the device activation bit is clear, or when the base address read is 0; in those cases it does not fill in *address. It returns 0 only after the base address is nonzero, having set *address, sio_data->sioaddr, revision, type and the skip_in, skip_pwm, skip_fan, skip_temp, skip_vid, internal, beep_pin, vid_value, need_in7_reroute, ec_special_config and smbus_bitmap fields from per-chip GPIO/pin registers (and may have written the PINX2 register to re-route VCCH5V to in7). Every path after the successful superio_enter reaches the exit label, which calls superio_exit(sioaddr, !enabled).
note: slice cut the head; packet name it87_sio_probe does not exist in it87.c, the function is it87_find (it87.c:2673-3194, head at 2673). Old prose claimed only that fields 'reflect' GPIO config and omitted the -ENODEV/err returns and exit cleanup.

name: LM93_IN_REL_TO_REG
prose: Precondition: vid * 1000 does not overflow int. Postcondition: uv_offset (a long) is initialised to vid * 1000 - val * 10000 evaluated in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic because val is unsigned, so on an LP64 target it is always a nonnegative value below 2^32 and on a 32-bit-long target it is that value reinterpreted as signed. If upper is nonzero, uv_offset is clamped to [12500, 200000] and the function returns (u8)((uv_offset / 12500 - 1) << 4). If upper is zero, uv_offset is clamped to [-400000, -25000] and the function returns (u8)(uv_offset / -25000 - 1): on a target where long is 64 bits the nonnegative uv_offset always clamps to -25000 so the result is 0, but where long is 32 bits a wrapped negative uv_offset can give a nonzero result in 0..15. It has no side effects.
note: reviewer was right: old prose claimed the lower branch always returns 0, which holds only for 64-bit long (lm93.c:392-404). Contract left empty: clamp_val and the arch-dependent long.

name: superio_enter
prose: Precondition: ioreg is the base I/O port of the Super-I/O index/data pair. Postcondition: if request_muxed_region(ioreg, 2, DRVNAME) fails it returns -EBUSY (-16) without writing to any port; otherwise it writes 0x87 twice to port ioreg with outb and returns 0, leaving the 2-port region reserved for the caller to release later.
note: reviewer round-2 claim that -EBUSY is -13 is wrong (EBUSY is 16, nct6683.c:97-111 returns -EBUSY). Contract dropped (I/O port side effects).

name: nct6775_asuswmi_write
prose: Precondition: none beyond the u8 argument types. Postcondition: it calls nct6775_asuswmi_evaluate_method(ASUSWMI_METHODID_WHWM, bank, reg, val, NULL) and returns its result unchanged: with CONFIG_ACPI it is 0 when acpi_evaluate_integer on the WMBD method succeeds and -EIO when it fails; without CONFIG_ACPI it is -EOPNOTSUPP. It takes no lock and allocates nothing; the result retval pointer is NULL so no value is stored.
note: nct6775-platform.c:162-166 and callee at 128-158. Prose was right; reviewer reasons were only the mechanical contract-omits-errno complaint, contract dropped because the result depends on a config option and global asus_acpi_dev.

name: bpa_rs600_read_vin
prose: Precondition: client is a valid i2c_client for the BPA-RS600. Postcondition: it reads the word PMBUS_READ_VIN with pmbus_read_word_data(client, 0, 0xff, ...) and returns a negative value from that call unchanged. Otherwise, if bit 10 of the word is clear it returns the word unchanged; if bit 10 is set it returns ((word >> 11) + 1) << 11 | ((word & 0x7ff) >> 1), which can be as large as 0x103ff when the exponent field is 31 (0x10000 | 0x3ff) and therefore does not always fit in 16 bits. It has no other side effects.
note: reviewer (round 15) was right: old prose said up to 0x107ff but the mantissa is shifted right by one, so the maximum is 0x103ff (bpa-rs600.c:42-57). Contract left empty (BIT macro, callee read).

name: max34451_set_supported_funcs
prose: Precondition: client is the i2c_client of a MAX34451-family device and data points to its max34440_data with info already initialised. Postcondition: it reads PMBUS_MFR_REVISION with i2c_smbus_read_word_data and returns the negative errno if that fails. If the revision is at least MAX34451ETNA6_MFR_REV it sets data->info.format, m, b and R for PSC_VOLTAGE_IN and PSC_CURRENT_IN (direct, m=1, b=0, R=3 and 2) and sets data->iout_oc_fault_limit and data->iout_oc_warn_limit. Then for each page 0..15 it writes PMBUS_PAGE (sleeping MAX34440_PAGE_CHANGE_DELAY after the write, before checking its result), returns the negative errno if the write failed, reads MAX34451_MFR_CHANNEL_CONFIG and returns the negative errno if that read failed, and sets data->info.func[page] by the selection field: 0x10 or 0x20 voltage out plus status, 0x21 voltage out, 0x22 current out plus status, 0x23 current out, adding the input flags when the revision was at least MAX34451ETNA6_MFR_REV; any other selection leaves func[page] unchanged. It returns 0 after all 16 pages. On an error return the earlier pages may already be updated, and PMBUS_PAGE is not restored. It takes no lock.
note: slice cut the head; real name max34451_set_supported_funcs (max34440.c:245-329). Old prose omitted the 0x23 selection and invented i2c_get_clientdata inside the function (data is a parameter).

name: sm_via686a_init
prose: Precondition: none; module init function. Postcondition: it returns pci_register_driver(&via686a_pci_driver) unchanged: 0 on success, a negative errno otherwise. via686a_pci_probe, which may run for matching PCI devices during registration, itself always returns -ENODEV (so probe results do not change this return value) but on its success path leaves a registered platform driver, platform device and an s_bridge reference that only sm_via686a_exit releases, and only when s_bridge is non-NULL.
note: via686a.c:920-923, probe at 850-908, exit at 925-933. Reviewer's claim that no probe can run on registration failure cannot be established from this function, so the prose says only that probe may run; prior claim 'in either case' removed.

name: set_pwm_auto_point_temp
prose: Precondition: dev's driver data is a valid vt1211_data, attr is a sensor_device_attribute_2 whose index (ix) selects pwm_ctl and whose nr (ap) indexes pwm_auto_temp, and buf is a NUL-terminated string. Postcondition: if kstrtol(buf, 10, &val) fails it returns that error without taking the lock or changing anything; otherwise it takes data->update_lock, reads VT1211_REG_PWM_CTL and refreshes data->pwm_ctl[0] and [1] from it, stores TEMP_TO_REG(data->pwm_ctl[ix] & 7, val) in data->pwm_auto_temp[ap], writes that value to VT1211_REG_PWM_AUTO_TEMP(ap) with vt1211_write8, releases the lock and returns count.
note: slice cut the head; packet name set_pwm_auto_temp does not exist, the function is set_pwm_auto_point_temp (vt1211.c:758-789).

name: fan_time_functions(fan_stop_time, W83627EHF_REG_FAN_STOP_TIME)
prose: Generated function store_fan_stop_time(dev, attr, buf, count) from the fan_time_functions macro instantiated for fan_stop_time. Precondition: dev's driver data is a valid w83627ehf_data, attr is a sensor_device_attribute whose index nr is a valid index into data->fan_stop_time, data->pwm_mode and W83627EHF_REG_FAN_STOP_TIME, and buf is a NUL-terminated string. Postcondition: if kstrtoul(buf, 10, &val) returns a negative value it returns that error before taking the lock; otherwise val becomes step_time_to_reg(val, data->pwm_mode[nr]) (a value clamped to 1..255, computed before the lock is taken), then under data->update_lock it stores it in data->fan_stop_time[nr] and writes it to W83627EHF_REG_FAN_STOP_TIME[nr] with w83627ehf_write_value, releases the lock and returns count.
note: packet name store_fan_step_time does not exist in w83627ehf.c; the only fan_time_functions instantiation is fan_stop_time (w83627ehf.c:993-1027), so the old prose used wrong field/register names. slice cut the head.

name: etm_event_stop
prose: Precondition: called on the CPU that owns the per-CPU etm_ctxt, with event and mode valid. Postcondition: if mode has PERF_EF_PAUSE it only returns etm_event_pause(path, event, ctxt) (a void call), changing nothing else here. Otherwise: if handle->event is set and perf_get_aux(handle) != ctxt->event_data it WARNs and returns before changing anything; else it reads ctxt->event_data and sets ctxt->event_data to NULL, and then returns without further work if event->hw.state is already PERF_HES_STOPPED or (after a WARN) if the saved event_data is NULL. If handle->event is set, PERF_EF_UPDATE is requested and this CPU is not in event_data->mask, it sets event->hw.state to PERF_HES_STOPPED, calls perf_aux_output_end(handle, 0) and returns. If the path has no source or no sink it returns, leaving the state and path untouched. Otherwise it disables the source, sets event->hw.state to PERF_HES_STOPPED and, when handle->event is set and PERF_EF_UPDATE is requested, returns early (path not disabled) after a WARN_ON_ONCE if handle->event != event or if the sink has no update_buffer op; otherwise it calls update_buffer with event_data->snk_config and ends the AUX handle with the returned size when handle->event is still set (WARN_ON(size) when it is not). Unless one of those earlier returns was taken, it finally calls coresight_disable_path(path).
note: reviewers were right that the old prose misdescribed the PAUSE return and path disabling; but the round-15 claim 'WARNs on == vs !=' is a misreading of the old precondition wording, code WARNs on != (coresight-etm-perf.c:~707, WARN_ON(perf_get_aux(handle) != ctxt->event_data)). Verified every return at lines 664-751.

name: reset_store
prose: Precondition: dev is an ETMv4 device whose parent holds a valid etmv4_drvdata, and buf is a NUL-terminated string. Postcondition: if kstrtoul(buf, 16, &val) fails it returns -EINVAL without changing anything. Otherwise, with drvdata->spinlock held (raw_spin_lock), it sets config->mode to 0 if val is nonzero, and in all cases (including val == 0) clears the load/store and data-trace mode and cfg bits, zeroes the event, timestamp, stall controls, ViewInst include/start-stop controls, the sequencer, external-input, counter, resource (from index 2), single-shot, address-comparator, context-ID and VMID configuration and their index fields, sets config->syncfreq to 0x8 only when drvdata->syncpr is false, and sets config->vinst_ctrl to FIELD_PREP(TRCVICTLR_EVENT_MASK, 0x01), additionally setting ETM_MODE_VIEWINST_STARTSTOP in config->mode and TRCVICTLR_SSSTATUS in vinst_ctrl when drvdata->nr_addr_cmp > 0. It then releases the spinlock, calls etm4_release_trace_id(drvdata) and cscfg_csdev_reset_feats(to_coresight_device(dev)) and returns size.
note: reviewer (round 15) claim 'reset_store clears vinst_ctrl' is wrong: coresight-etm4x-sysfs.c line ~185 sets vinst_ctrl = FIELD_PREP(TRCVICTLR_EVENT_MASK, 0x01) unconditionally and ORs in SSSTATUS only if nr_addr_cmp > 0; old prose wrongly tied the event mask to the comparator condition, and omitted that val == 0 still resets everything except mode. Verified all returns (kstrtoul failure and final).

name: tmc_panic_sync_etf
prose: Precondition: csdev is a valid coresight device whose parent's drvdata is an initialised tmc_drvdata. Postcondition: both of its return statements return 0. If tmc_has_reserved_buffer(drvdata) or tmc_has_crash_mdata_buffer(drvdata) is false it returns 0 immediately without touching hardware or metadata. Otherwise it marks the crash metadata invalid with tmc_crashdata_set_invalid, calls CS_UNLOCK(drvdata->base) (the CoreSight unlock-access macro; no mutex or spinlock is taken), reads TMC_CTL and, if TMC_CTL_CAPT_EN is clear, or reads TMC_MODE and it is not TMC_MODE_CIRCULAR_BUFFER, jumps to the out label. When capture is enabled in circular-buffer mode it does a manual flush and stop (tmc_flush_and_stop) unless TMC_FFSR_FT_STOPPED is already set, in which case it waits for TMC ready, copies TMC_STS, TMC_MODE, TMC_FFCR and TMC_FFSR into the metadata, sets drvdata->buf to the reserved buffer and dumps the internal SRAM into it with tmc_etb_dump_hw, fills in the ram size, rrp, dba, rwp, trace physical address and version fields, issues dmb(sy), sets mdata->valid to true, computes crc32_tdata then crc32_mdata, and calls tmc_disable_hw. The out label then calls CS_UNLOCK(drvdata->base) a second time (not CS_LOCK) and returns 0.
note: reviewers (round 2 and 15) were right: old prose called CS_UNLOCK 'taking the device lock' and said it was 'released again' before returning, but out: calls CS_UNLOCK again and CS_LOCK is never called (coresight-tmc-etf.c:604-677).

name: intel_th_msc_interrupt
prose: Precondition: thdev is an intel_th_device whose driver data is a valid struct msc with its MSU register window mapped. Postcondition: it returns IRQ_NONE at once, reading nothing further, if msc->do_irq is clear or msc->mbuf is NULL. Otherwise it reads REG_MSU_MSUSTS and masks it with the MSC0BLAST or MSC1BLAST bit chosen by msc->index; if no masked bit is set it returns IRQ_HANDLED when msc->enabled is set and IRQ_NONE when it is clear. If bits are set it writes them back to MSUSTS to clear them, returns IRQ_NONE if msc->enabled is clear, returns IRQ_HANDLED if msc->cur_win is NULL or msc_next_window() returns NULL, and if msc_win_set_lockout(next_win, WIN_READY, WIN_INUSE) returns nonzero it either schedules msc->work (when msc->stop_on_full) or stores next_win in msc->switch_on_unlock and returns IRQ_HANDLED. When the lockout succeeds it moves the current window WIN_INUSE to WIN_LOCKED, calls msc_win_switch(msc), calls msc->mbuf->ready(msc->mbuf_priv, win->sgt, msc_win_total_sz(win)) if msc->mbuf and its ready op are non-NULL, and returns IRQ_HANDLED. It takes no lock itself.
note: slice cut the head; packet name msu_irq_handler does not exist, the function is intel_th_msc_interrupt (msu.c:1762-1810). Old prose missed the first early IRQ_NONE return (!do_irq || !mbuf).

name: nr_pages_store
prose: Precondition: dev's driver data is a valid struct msc and buf holds size bytes. Postcondition: it returns -EPERM without CAP_SYS_RAWIO, and returns the nonzero result of msc_buffer_free_unless_used(msc) if that fails (the old buffer is freed only when it is not in use). It then parses the part of buf before the first newline as a comma-separated list of decimal numbers, copying each token with kstrndup (returning -ENOMEM through free_win if that fails), converting it with kstrtoul and stopping at the first conversion error (that error is returned) or at a token whose value is 0 (the function then returns size and allocates no buffer); a second window when msc->mode is MSC_MODE_SINGLE gives -EINVAL, and a failure of krealloc_array frees the array and returns -ENOMEM directly. If the whole list parses it takes msc->buf_mutex, calls msc_buffer_alloc(msc, win, nr_wins), releases the mutex, frees the temporary array and returns size on success or the allocation error otherwise. The temporary window array is freed on every return after the loop starts, and buf_mutex is held only around msc_buffer_alloc.
note: reviewer (round 15) is wrong: the real code uses kstrndup and kstrtoul (msu.c:1986-2040: s = kstrndup(p, end ? end - p : len, GFP_KERNEL); ret = kstrtoul(s, 10, &val)), so the -ENOMEM/kstrtoul claims in the old prose were correct; prose rewritten for the zero-value return and the direct -ENOMEM return. name was outside the slice (head at msu.c:1986).

name: pca_xfer
prose: Precondition: i2c_adap->algo_data points to a valid i2c_algo_pca_data whose callbacks are set, msgs has at least num valid messages when num > 0, and i2c_adap->timeout is set. Postcondition: it polls the status with pca_status, sleeping 10 ms between polls, until it reads 0xf8 (idle) and returns -EBUSY if the status is still not 0xf8 when jiffies passes the timeout. It then, while curmsg < num, drives the controller by status: 0xf8 starts, 0x08/0x10 sends the address, 0x18/0x28 sends the next byte or moves to the next message (stop after the last), 0x40/0x50/0x58 handle reads, and unrecognised statuses log an error and loop again if the last helper's completion flag is still set. If the loop ends normally it returns curmsg, which equals num after all messages are done and is 0 when num <= 0 because the loop body is skipped; otherwise it returns -ENXIO after a NACK on SLA+W (0x20) or SLA+R (0x48) (after pca_stop), and the default -EIO after a NACK on a data byte (0x30), arbitration loss (0x38), a non-final read byte NACKed (0x58 with numbytes != len - 1), bus errors (0x70, 0x78, 0x90, 0x00, after pca_reset) or when a helper such as pca_start/pca_address/pca_tx_byte reports not completed. It acquires no locks or references.
note: reviewer claims (rounds 1-15) are all mostly wrong about the prior prose: for num <= 0 the code returns 0 because ret = curmsg = 0 (i2c-algo-pca.c, ret = curmsg after the loop), and the non-final read NACK does goto out with the initial ret = -EIO. Prose tightened to enumerate the status cases. Verified all returns at lines 1267 and 1421.

name: i2c_davinci_isr
prose: Precondition: dev_id is the davinci_i2c_dev registered for this interrupt. Postcondition: if pm_runtime_suspended(dev->dev) it returns IRQ_NONE without reading registers. Otherwise it repeatedly reads DAVINCI_I2C_IVR_REG until it reads 0; on the 101st nonzero read it warns and breaks before handling that event, so at most 100 events are handled. For each event: AL sets DAVINCI_I2C_STR_AL in dev->cmd_err, zeroes dev->buf_len and completes dev->cmd_complete; NACK does the same with DAVINCI_I2C_STR_NACK; neither clears or masks a status or interrupt bit. ARDY writes DAVINCI_I2C_STR_ARDY to the status register, sets the STP bit in MDR when (buf_len == 0 and dev->stop != 0) or cmd_err has the NACK bit, and completes cmd_complete. RDR reads DRR into *dev->buf++ and decrements buf_len (continuing with the next IVR read while buf_len is still nonzero, otherwise writing DAVINCI_I2C_IMR_RRDY to the status register), or calls terminate_read when buf_len is already 0. XRDY writes *dev->buf++ to DXR and decrements buf_len (continuing while nonzero, otherwise clearing the XRDY bit in the interrupt mask register), or calls terminate_write when buf_len is 0. SCD writes DAVINCI_I2C_STR_SCD to the status register and completes cmd_complete. AAS only logs and unrecognised statuses only warn. It returns IRQ_HANDLED if at least one nonzero IVR value was read (including the one that triggered the break) and IRQ_NONE otherwise.
note: reviewers right: AL/NACK do not clear or mask a status bit (old prose said they did) and at most 100 events are handled; the first reviewer's 'suspended' complaint was already handled in the old prose. i2c-davinci.c:578-651.

name: i801_isr_byte_done
prose: Precondition: priv describes an in-progress interrupt-driven block transfer; for reads priv->len may still be SMBUS_LEN_SENTINEL and priv->data points at data->block[1] so priv->data[-1] is writable. Postcondition: it returns nothing. If priv->is_read is set: when priv->len == SMBUS_LEN_SENTINEL it replaces it with i801_get_block_len(priv) (or I2C_SMBUS_BLOCK_MAX if that is negative) and stores the result in priv->data[-1]; then if priv->count < priv->len it reads one byte from SMBBLKDAT into priv->data[priv->count] and increments priv->count, otherwise it discards the byte (reading nothing, leaving count unchanged); finally if priv->count == priv->len - 1 it writes priv->cmd | SMBHSTCNT_LAST_BYTE to SMBHSTCNT. If priv->is_read is clear, only when priv->count < priv->len - 1 it increments priv->count and writes priv->data[priv->count] to SMBBLKDAT. Nothing else is changed.
note: reviewer (round 1) claim that count does not advance on a discarded byte is consistent with the old prose and code (i2c-i801.c:559-575); prose kept with small cleanup (the extra byte is not read at all, 'Discarding extra byte' only logs).

name: i801_block_transaction_byte_by_byte
prose: Precondition: priv is initialised, data->block[0] holds the block length (SMBUS_LEN_SENTINEL for reads whose length is learned from the device) and data->block[1..] the data for writes. Postcondition: it returns -EOPNOTSUPP if command is I2C_SMBUS_BLOCK_PROC_CALL. For writes it first writes the length to SMBHSTDAT0 and block[1] to SMBBLKDAT. With FEATURE_IRQ it sets priv->is_read, cmd, len, count and data, re-initialises priv->done, writes SMBHSTCNT with START and interrupts enabled, waits up to adap->timeout and returns priv->status (0 or a positive error-flag mask set by the interrupt handler) or -ETIMEDOUT if the wait expired. Without FEATURE_IRQ it starts the transfer and for each byte calls i801_wait_byte_done and returns its nonzero result (a positive error-flag mask or -ETIMEDOUT) at once; for a sentinel length it reads the real length with i801_get_block_len, and if that is negative it spins writing SMBHSTSTS_BYTE_DONE while SMBHSTSTS_HOST_BUSY is set, writes SMBHSTSTS_INTR and returns -EPROTO, otherwise it stores the length in data->block[0]; reads fill data->block[i], and the last-byte flag is set when i == len - 1. After the loop it returns i801_wait_intr(priv), which is 0, a positive error-flag mask or -ETIMEDOUT. Only the sentinel-length failure path drains the hardware; no lock or reference is taken.
note: reviewer (round 1) was right: old prose said wait_byte_done/wait_intr return negative errno, but they return positive error-flag masks too (i2c-i801.c:345-376), and only the -EPROTO path drains hardware. Verified returns at 663-731.

name: mlxbf_i2c_smbus_write_data
prose: Precondition: round_up(length, 4) fits in the u8 aligned_length (length <= 252), data points to a 4-byte aligned buffer with at least round_up(length, 4) readable bytes, and addr plus the offsets stay inside the mapped register window of the selected block (priv->mst->io when is_master is true, priv->slv->io otherwise). Postcondition: it reads round_up(length, 4) / 4 32-bit words from data and writes each with iowrite32be to the selected block at addr, addr + 4, ... up to addr + aligned_length - 4. Bytes beyond length within the last word are read from the buffer and written to the registers as well. It returns nothing and takes no lock.
note: reviewer (round 15) was right: old prose said bytes past length are ignored but the loop writes whole words (i2c-mlxbf.c:577-603).

name: mtk_i2c_transfer
prose: Precondition: adap's adapdata is an initialised mtk_i2c and msgs holds num valid i2c_msg entries. Postcondition: it enables the bulk clocks first and returns the nonzero result of clk_bulk_enable if that fails, with no clock left enabled by this call. After a successful enable every return goes through err_exit, which calls clk_bulk_disable. A two-message write-then-read to the same address is merged into one I2C_MASTER_WRRD transaction (auto_restart cleared). Messages are processed one transaction at a time; before each, a NULL buf in the current message (only the first message of a merged pair is checked here) gives -EINVAL, and the first negative result of mtk_i2c_do_transfer is returned as is, stopping the loop. If every transaction succeeds it returns num.
note: reviewers right on early exit and success value; reviewer claims about -ENOMEM for the second message's NULL buf cannot be asserted from this function (the buffer is handled inside mtk_i2c_do_transfer), so the prose says only that the negative result of mtk_i2c_do_transfer is propagated (i2c-mt65xx.c:1238-1278).

name: npcm_i2c_master_xfer
prose: Precondition: msgs[0] is valid, and msgs[1] is valid when msgs[0] is a write and num == 2; the i2c core serialises transfers. Postcondition: it returns -EINVAL before touching the hardware if bus->state is I2C_DISABLE or if the computed write or read length is 32 KiB or more. Otherwise it polls the busy bit for about adap.timeout / adap.retries + 1 jiffies, taking bus->lock with spin_lock_irqsave around each poll; during these polls, when CONFIG_I2C_SLAVE is on, a slave is registered and the bus is not busy, it writes the slave address (without the enable bit) to NPCM_I2CADDR1. It then sets bus->dest_addr and, if the bus is still busy or bus->ber_state is set, writes NPCM_I2CCST_BB to clear the busy bit, resets the module, calls i2c_recover_bus() and returns -EAGAIN. Otherwise it initialises the transfer state, enables interrupts, starts the transfer, and if npcm_i2c_master_start_xmit succeeds waits for completion up to the computed timeout; on timeout and in master mode it runs i2c_recover_bus(), sets bus->cmd_err to -EIO and bus->state to I2C_IDLE. A cmd_err of -EAGAIN is replaced by the return value of i2c_recover_bus(); another nonzero cmd_err with the last-PEC bit set in NPCM_I2CRXF_CTL resets the module. It then disables stall-after-start and EOB interrupts and, with CONFIG_I2C_SLAVE and a registered slave, rewrites its address with the enable bit (without CONFIG_I2C_SLAVE it disables interrupts instead), and returns bus->cmd_err, which is 0 on success or the errno stored by the transfer, timeout or recovery handling.
note: reviewers right in two points: the -EAGAIN return can follow a slave-address write in the busy poll (round 15), and cmd_err after a BER is the i2c_recover_bus() result (round 2); old prose also said cmd_err was only 0/-EIO/recover, but the interrupt handler can store other errnos. i2c-npcm7xx.c:2288-2354.
